notes: User cancels a long in-flight Copilot turn, then issues a recovery prompt that proves the parser reset. INTERRUPT BINDING: Copilot CLI 1.0.77 binds interrupt to esc-esc within a 500 ms window (app.js: `let ye=500`; the first Escape only arms the intent, the second within the window calls interruptMainTurn) — the driver's interrupt arm must send BOTH presses in one tmux call, which is this cell's driver gap. WHAT IS ASSERTED: the user-observable arc only — ready→working→ready, state does NOT stick in working post-interrupt, and the session never enters waiting. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: any interrupt-attributed transition. ParsedEvent.IsUserInterrupt is set in exactly one place in the tree (claudecode/parser.go:385, off the literal '[Request interrupted by user]' marker); the copilot parser sets it nowhere, so LastWasUserInterrupt never becomes true and the classifier's rule-3 'user ESC interrupt' branch cannot fire for Copilot — same call as the pi and aider rows of this scenario. PROVISIONAL: whether the ABORTED turn writes its own assistant.turn_end could not be established from the shipped bundle (the local turn-end emit is a native bridge callback; the relay session class does emit it durably on abort). If it does, `recovery_done` is satisfied at the interrupt itself; if it does not, the recovery prompt's turn_end carries it (pi's shape). The spec passes under both, and `record` must report which by counting '"type":"assistant.turn_end"' lines in the frozen transcript. PRESESSION SHAPE: copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a proc-<PID> row (1s poll) before the fswatcher sees any transcript; the real session then arrives under a DIFFERENT id. Birth is modeled as two phases and every post-birth phase is anchored to the REAL session (templated from the copilot basic-turn row). HOW RUNS DIFFER: the essay wording, how much streamed before the cancel, per-turn token counts and sub-second timing all vary; stable structurally is one ready→working→ready arc on one real session id that never enters waiting and ends ready. OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map (session.usage_checkpoint carries no token counts — only shutdown does). model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn.
